title: Stale reads caused by process pausing
body: In an Antithesis robustness run on the main branch, one etcd member's revision stopped progressing for a long time, but that member continued accepting reads and writes. The resulting history is not linearizable: the linearizability checker flags the run as inconsistent. I attached the report, state dump, and a screenshot. Configuration includes ETCD_SNAPSHOT_CATCHUP_ENTRIES=100, ETCD_SNAPSHOT_COUNT=50, and ETCD_COMPACTION_BATCH_LIMIT=10.

symptoms_visible: In an Antithesis run, one member's revision stopped progressing for a long time while it continued accepting reads and writes, and the resulting client history was not linearizable.
N0.label: N0 stale-read failure reported

symptoms_visible: For key26 with value 147, one client received revision 3 while other clients' watches recorded the same operation at revision 155.
N1.label: N1 linearizability violation clarified

symptoms_visible: A transaction completed at proposed index 11, then 460 ms later a Range request started on another member and ultimately used read index 10.
N2.label: N2 ordered read-index evidence collected

symptoms_visible: One of three Antithesis runs on the branch with the leadership/select-race patch still produced a failed linearization assertion.
N2_x.label: N2_x early leadership-race fix aftermath

symptoms_visible: The instrumented failing run still returned stale data after a process stall; its trace contains repeated ReadIndex sends with the same request ID and delayed heartbeat processing around other queued reads.
N3.label: N3 duplicate ReadIndex trace captured

symptoms_visible: The instrumented unfixed builds reproduced the failed linearization assertion, while four initial runs with the fresh-request-ID patch and five consecutive periodic CI runs completed without finding it.
N4.label: N4 fresh-ID patch verified under fault injection

symptoms_visible: Antithesis and periodic robustness runs containing the fix complete without reproducing the stale-read linearization failure.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: What exact client operations make this history non-linearizable?
Can you explain what the Porcupine failure shows for a specific key?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: For key26 with value 147, client-4's watch and client-6's operation record show revision 3, while the other clients' watch files show the same put at revision 155.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: All clients show the operation at the same revision; the only discrepancy is delayed watch delivery.
The same mismatch appears on a different key and value, with one client far behind the others.

edges.comment: The exact client-side mismatch was extracted by another maintainer from the shared Antithesis artifacts. Contributors investigating the same failure are folded into one simulated user side.

question_patterns: Can you instrument the write and Range request boundaries and provide their ordered timestamps and indexes?
Do the logs prove that the stale read began after the write completed?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The Antithesis log has the Txn completion at 23.731 with revision 4 and proposed-index 11, followed by the Range request start at 24.193. I initially quoted the wrong interval; the relevant difference is about 460 ms.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The Range request began before the transaction completed, so this trace does not show a read that started after the write.
The ordered interval is 430 ms rather than 460 ms, but the Range request still starts after the completed write.

question_patterns: What ReadIndex did that Range request receive?
Please add read-index logging and quote the response associated with the stale Range request.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The request started at 24.193. At 24.870 it sent ReadIndex request 7179191402480470886, and at 25.817 it received index 10.

question_patterns: What faults did Antithesis inject around the failure?
Can you clarify what the pause, throttle, slowed partition, and jammed-network events do?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The run includes docker pause/unpause events, a slowed network partition between container groups, a jammed link with a throughput limit, and CPU throttling of a container. A node pause normally pauses its container for about two seconds before unpausing it.

question_patterns: Can timestamps from different containers in the Antithesis event log be compared reliably?
Do the simulation timestamps preserve the global event order?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, we can trust the time and order of the Antithesis logs.

edges.comment: Instrumentation and fault interpretation came from the reporter and Antithesis participant. This is a measurement edge: it collects raw timestamps, indexes, and fault definitions without assigning the root cause.

solution.intent: Treat the stale ReadIndex as a race between the ReadState and leadership-change select cases, and patch the leadership check before accepting the result.
solution.concrete_example: Change the select/leadership handling so a ReadState is not accepted when a concurrent leadership-change notification is ready, then rerun Antithesis.

edges.comment: The reporter explicitly labeled this an early blind guess. One of three subsequent Antithesis runs reproduced the linearization failure on the branch containing the proposed fix.

question_patterns: Can you instrument the raft ReadIndex request context through retries and show whether each retry gets a fresh ID?
Please log ReadIndex sends, receives, queue insertion, and heartbeat responses around another failure.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In the failing trace, etcd0 sent ReadIndex with request ID 3744633826720154659 at 16.725, then retried at 17.225 and 17.728 with that exact same ID. After a leader change it sent a new ID, 3744633826720154677.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every retry has a distinct request ID, including retries to the same leader.
The same request-ID reuse appears with different numeric IDs in another failing run.

question_patterns: What does the instrumented readOnly queue show when delayed responses and retried contexts are processed?
Can you quote the queue events around the repeated request ID and the later client read?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The logs show request 3744633826720154659 queued at read index 26, dequeued after a delayed heartbeat response, and then received and queued again after another client request was already in the queue. A later delayed response with that same request ID is processed while the newer request is queued.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The repeated context is discarded and never re-enters the queue; delayed responses do not coincide with any newer queued request.

edges.comment: The reporter added progressively deeper raft/readOnly logging. The answers preserve the raw IDs and queue events; concluding how those events validate a stale index is engineer-side inference reserved for the final solution.

question_patterns: Can you run long Antithesis tests with the patch that generates a fresh ReadIndex request ID for every retry?
After merging the fresh-ID patch, do periodic robustness runs still reproduce the failed linearization assertion?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Before the patch, two of three instrumented runs detected the issue. With commit 05c978844f47a09b4731723b9e6fa638e1f16f85, zero of four initial runs detected it. After merge, I ran the periodic job plus three additional copies, and CI then recorded five consecutive passes since March 2 with no failure.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: A long run with the fresh-request-ID patch still reproduces the same stale-read linearization failure.
Zero of five patched runs detected the issue instead of zero of four, followed by the same clean periodic results.

edges.comment: These are fault-injection and CI verification measurements. The user reports only run counts and assertion outcomes, not a stronger proof that absence of reproduction alone establishes the mechanism.

solution.intent: Prevent stale linearizable reads by generating a fresh ReadIndex RequestCtx/request ID for every retry, so delayed responses for an earlier attempt cannot interact with a newly queued request under the same context.
solution.concrete_example: Apply the change from PR 21399 so requestCurrentIndex allocates a new request index on every ReadIndex retry rather than reusing the previous context. Verify it with extended Antithesis fault-injection and periodic robustness runs before declaring the stale-read issue resolved.
solution.inference_hint: The raw trace only states that etcd reused a ReadIndex context, that delayed heartbeat responses arrived, and that queue entries were dequeued and requeued. The root-cause conclusion is that reuse violates the uniqueness assumption behind raft's readOnly queue: an old response for context A can advance the queue after A has been inserted again, validating a newer queued read without a quorum confirmation appropriate to that read and returning a stale cached commit index. That mechanism is engineer inference from the instrumentation.

edges.comment: The stable-release mitigation merged as PR 21399 and was verified by extended Antithesis and periodic runs. Broader raft API or queue redesign options were discussed separately, but the scored fix for this etcd issue is fresh RequestCtx generation on every retry.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause: etcd reused the same ReadIndex RequestCtx/request ID when retrying against the same leader, allowing delayed responses for that context to interact with raft's readOnly queue and release a stale read index.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the ordered write/read evidence and the instrumented trace showing repeated request IDs, delayed heartbeat processing, and readOnly queue activity.
The fix must generate a fresh ReadIndex request ID for every retry, preventing an old response from being associated with a newly queued use of the same context.
Must not present the leadership-change/select race patch as the resolution; that attempted fix was followed by another in-case reproduction.
Must require extended Antithesis or equivalent fault-injection verification and clean periodic runs before treating the issue as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Expert etcd maintainer and robustness-test investigator; comfortable instrumenting Go and raft internals, using Delve and Antithesis multiverse debugging, reading WAL/database artifacts, and running long fault-injection campaigns.
persona_hint.communication_style: Technical, direct, and iterative; posts extensive raw logs and commit links, corrects timing mistakes openly, labels uncertain ideas as guesses, and waits for repeated simulation evidence before accepting a fix.
